steps.title: Cell division
steps.body: is how organisms grow and repair damaged tissues. New cells are produced when existing cells divide. In humans, this happens constantly - for example, your skin cells divide every few hours to replace worn-out cells.

steps.title: Chromosomes
steps.body: are structures in the nucleus that contain DNA (genetic material). Human body cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). Sex cells (gametes) have 23 chromosomes (one of each pair).

steps.title: The cell cycle
steps.body: is the series of stages a cell goes through to grow and divide. It has three main stages: growth, DNA replication, and mitosis.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When describing the cell cycle, mention growth, DNA replication AND mitosis - all three stages "Two genetically identical daughter cells" - always say "identical" when describing mitosis Don't confuse mitosis with meiosis - mitosis produces identical cells; meiosis produces gametes For stem cell ethics questions, always give both sides of the argument Remember: bone marrow transplant = adult stem cells (not embryonic) Exam questions often ask you to "discuss" ethical issues - this means give arguments for AND against
